Key terms used throughout the hexkit documentation, in alphabetical order.
Each entry links to the chapter that covers the term in depth.

## Adapter

The code that connects a port of the application core to a piece of infrastructure.
In the Triple Hexagonal Architecture, an adapter is split into a translator and a provider.
See [Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/hexagonal_arch.qmd#adapters).

## At-least-once delivery

The guarantee of the Kafka subscriber: an event is never skipped, but it may be delivered more than once if the service stops before committing its offset.
Translators must therefore be idempotent.
See [Kafka Event Subscriber](../providers/kafka/subscriber.qmd#offset-management).

## Broker

The server that stores events and passes them from producers to consumers.
hexkit uses Apache Kafka as its broker.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd).

## Composition root

The one module of a service, conventionally `inject.py`, that knows which adapter implements which port and wires them together.
See [Dependency Injection](../arch_concepts/dependency_injection.qmd#the-composition-root).

## Config prefix

The `prefix` passed to `config_from_yaml`.
It names the config YAML file (`.{prefix}.yaml`) and prefixes the environment variables that hold the settings.
See [Configuration](../configuration.qmd#the-prefix).

## Consumer

A service that reads events from a topic, without knowing which service produced them.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd).

## Consumer group

The set of service instances that share the work of consuming a topic, so each event is processed by one instance only.
The Kafka subscriber uses the configured `service_name` as the consumer group ID.
See [Kafka Event Subscriber](../providers/kafka/subscriber.qmd).

## Core

The domain logic of a service, written in the language of the domain and free of infrastructure details.
It talks to the outside only through ports.
See [Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/hexagonal_arch.qmd#application-core-the-inside).

## Correlation ID

A UUID4 attached to a request chain at its origin and passed along in event headers and log records, so that all work belonging to one request can be found across services.
Also called a request ID.
See [Correlation IDs](../observability_tools/correlation_ids.qmd).

## DAO (data access object)

An object that offers CRUD and find operations for one resource type, independent of the database behind it.
hexkit defines it with the `Dao` protocol and creates instances through a DAO factory.
See [The DAO Pattern](../arch_concepts/dao_pattern.qmd) and [Data Access Objects](../protocols/dao.qmd).

## DAO factory

The object that creates DAOs, one per resource type, from a name, a DTO model and an ID field.
`MongoDbDaoFactory` is the MongoDB implementation.
See [Data Access Objects](../protocols/dao.qmd).

## DAO publisher

A DAO that also publishes an outbox event for every insert, update, upsert or delete.
It implements the producing side of the outbox pattern.
See [DAO Publisher](../protocols/daopublisher.qmd).

## DAO subscriber

A translator that consumes outbox events and receives each change through one of two methods: `changed()` or `deleted()`.
It implements the consuming side of the outbox pattern.
See [DAO Subscriber](../protocols/daosubscriber.qmd).

## Database version

The version number that the MongoDB migration tooling stores in a dedicated collection of the service's database.
Version 1 marks the start of versioning, so the first migration a service writes is version 2.
See [MongoDB Migrations](../providers/mongodb_migrations.qmd#how-versioning-works).

## Dead letter queue (DLQ)

The topic to which the Kafka subscriber publishes an event that still fails after all retries, instead of crashing the service.
The event keeps its payload, type and key and receives headers describing the failure.
See [Dead Letter Queue](../arch_concepts/dlq.qmd).

## Dependency injection

A way of building a service in which an object receives the objects it works with from outside, instead of creating them itself.
In a hexkit service, the composition root creates the adapters and passes them to the core.
See [Dependency Injection](../arch_concepts/dependency_injection.qmd).

## DTO (data transfer object)

A Pydantic model that describes the shape of the data a DAO stores or an event carries.
See [The DAO Pattern](../arch_concepts/dao_pattern.qmd).

## Event

A message that a producer publishes to a topic on a broker.
In hexkit, an event has a topic, a type, a key, a payload and headers, such as the correlation ID and the event ID.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd).

## Event ID

A UUID4 in an event's headers that identifies one event instance.
An event republished from the DLQ receives a new event ID.
See [Dead Letter Queue](../arch_concepts/dlq.qmd).

## Event type

A header field that hexkit adds to every event to tell different kinds of events on the same topic apart.
Outbox events use the types `upserted` and `deleted`.
See [DAO Publisher](../protocols/daopublisher.qmd#event-semantics).

## Event-driven architecture

A way for services to communicate in which a producer publishes events to a broker and consumers read them, instead of calling each other directly.
The producer does not know who consumes its events, and consumers do not know who produced them.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd).

## Fixture

Test setup that hexkit provides as pytest fixtures to run tests against real or in-memory infrastructure, such as `KafkaFixture`, `MongoDbFixture` and `S3Fixture`.
See [Kafka Test Utils](../providers/kafka/test_utils.qmd), [MongoDB Test Utils](../providers/mongodb.qmd#mongodb-test-utils) and [S3 Object Storage Test Utils](../providers/s3.qmd#s3-object-storage-test-utils).

## Headers

Metadata that travels with an event, separate from its payload.
The Kafka publisher always sets the headers `type`, `event_id` and `correlation_id`; a service may add more.
See [Kafka Event Publisher](../providers/kafka/publisher.qmd#headers-and-correlation-ids).

## Hexagonal Architecture

An architecture in which the core of a service depends only on ports, and adapters connect those ports to the outside world.
Also called Ports and Adapters; the Triple Hexagonal Architecture extends it.
See [Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/hexagonal_arch.qmd).

## Idempotence

The property of a consumer that processing the same event twice leaves the service in the same state as processing it once.
hexkit consumers must be idempotent, because events can be redelivered and republished.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd#implications).

## Inbound and outbound

The direction of a port or adapter, seen from the core.
An inbound port is called by the outside world, such as a REST endpoint or an event subscriber; an outbound port is called by the core, such as a DAO or an event publisher.
See [Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/hexagonal_arch.qmd#ports).

## Key

The value that decides which partition of a topic an event goes to.
Kafka keeps events in order only within a partition, so events with the same key keep their order; outbox events use the resource ID as the key.

## Key-value store

Storage that saves and retrieves values by a string key, defined by the `KeyValueStoreProtocol`.
Providers exist for Redis, MongoDB, S3, Vault and in-memory testing, each in a `Bytes`, `Str`, `Json` and `Dto` variant.
See [Protocols](../protocols/index.qmd#keyvaluestoreprotocol).

## Migration

Code that converts the documents of a MongoDB database from one database version to the next, written as a `MigrationDefinition` subclass.
The `MigrationManager` runs pending migrations once, even when several service instances start at the same time.
See [MongoDB Migrations](../providers/mongodb_migrations.qmd).

## Multipart upload

An upload that splits a large file into parts, each uploaded through its own presigned URL, and then completes them into one object.
For a smaller file, a single presigned POST request is enough.
See [Object Storage](../protocols/objstorage.qmd#multipart-uploads).

## Object storage

Storage for files organized in buckets, defined by the `ObjectStorageProtocol`.
File content moves through presigned URLs, not through the service.
See [Object Storage](../protocols/objstorage.qmd).

## Offset

The position of a consumer group within a topic.
The Kafka subscriber commits the offset only after an event has been fully handled.
See [Kafka Event Subscriber](../providers/kafka/subscriber.qmd#offset-management).

## Outbox pattern

A way to share data between services: the owning service stores a resource and publishes its full latest state as an event, and other services keep their own copy by consuming those events.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd#outbox-pattern).

## Partition

A subdivision of a Kafka topic.
Kafka keeps events in order within a partition, and events with the same key always go to the same partition.
See [Kafka Event Publisher](../providers/kafka/publisher.qmd).

## Payload

The data an event carries, as a JSON object.
Consumers usually validate it against a Pydantic model.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd).

## Persistent publisher

An event publisher, `PersistentKafkaPublisher`, that stores every event in MongoDB as it publishes it, so the same event can be published again later.
Unlike the DAO publisher, it publishes arbitrary events, not resource states.
See [Outbox vs. Persistent Publisher](../developer_help/outbox_v_persistent_pub.qmd).

## Port

An interface of the core, written in the language of the domain, through which the core is called or calls out.
See [Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/hexagonal_arch.qmd#ports).

## Presigned URL

A time-limited URL that lets a client upload or download an object directly from object storage, without credentials of its own.
See [Object Storage](../protocols/objstorage.qmd).

## Producer

A service that publishes events to a topic, without knowing which services consume them.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd).

## Protocol

An abstract interface for one type of infrastructure, such as a DAO or an event publisher, that does not depend on a specific technology.
It separates the translator from the provider.
See [Protocols](../protocols/index.qmd) and [Triple Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/triple_hexagonal_arch.qmd#the-core-concept).

## Provider

The technology-specific implementation of a protocol, such as `MongoDbDaoFactory` for the DAO protocol or `KafkaEventPublisher` for the event publisher protocol.
Providers are general-purpose and shared across services.
See [Providers](../providers/index.qmd).

## Republish

Publishing stored events again: the DAO publisher and the persistent publisher both offer `republish()` for this.
The DAO publisher sends the current state of all its resources, for example to fill a newly deployed consumer service.
Republished events receive new event IDs but keep their stored correlation IDs.
See [Outbox vs. Persistent Publisher](../developer_help/outbox_v_persistent_pub.qmd#republishing).

## Retry topic

The topic `retry-<service_name>` to which an event from the DLQ is republished for another attempt.
The Kafka subscriber restores the original topic name before passing the event to the translator.
See [Dead Letter Queue](../arch_concepts/dlq.qmd#republishing-and-re-consuming-dlq-events).

## Span

One recorded operation in OpenTelemetry tracing, with its timing, attributes and outcome.
Spans form a trace through their parent spans.
See [OpenTelemetry](../observability_tools/opentelemetry.qmd).

## Tombstone

The `deleted` outbox event: an event with an empty payload whose key names the deleted resource.
See [DAO Publisher](../protocols/daopublisher.qmd).

## Topic

A named stream of events on the broker.
A topic can have any number of producers and consumers, and events stay on it after they are consumed.

## Topic compaction

A Kafka setting that keeps only the latest event per key in a topic.
Combined with the outbox pattern, a consumer that reads a compacted topic receives the current state of every resource.
See [Event-driven Architecture](../arch_concepts/event_driven_arch.qmd#outbox-pattern).

## Trace

The tree of spans that follows one request across services in OpenTelemetry tracing.
hexkit passes the trace context in event headers, so a trace continues across the broker.
Unlike a correlation ID, a trace also records timing and which operation caused which.
See [OpenTelemetry](../observability_tools/opentelemetry.qmd#traces-across-kafka-events).

## Translator

The service-specific inner part of an adapter, which converts between a port of the core and a protocol.
A Kafka event subscriber, for example, passes each event to a translator that implements `EventSubscriberProtocol`.
See [Triple Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/triple_hexagonal_arch.qmd#the-core-concept).

## Triple Hexagonal Architecture

An extension of the Hexagonal Architecture that adds the protocol as a third interface, splitting each adapter into a translator and a provider.
Providers can then be shared across services.
See [Triple Hexagonal Architecture](../arch_concepts/triple_hexagonal_arch.qmd).

## Upsert

A write that updates a resource if it exists and inserts it otherwise.
The `Dao` offers it as `upsert()`, next to `insert()`, which fails if the resource exists, and `update()`, which fails if it does not.
See [Data Access Objects](../protocols/dao.qmd#crud-operations).
